findings.claim: Databricks' annualized revenue reached $6.9B in June 2026 (growing >80% YoY), surpassing Snowflake's ~$5.6B annualized revenue; Databricks first passed Snowflake in the October 2025 quarter and the gap has widened every quarter since. Snowflake's growth rate over the same period was ~34-37% YoY, roughly half Databricks' pace.
findings.source: CNBC "Databricks revenue growth tops 80% to $6.9 billion annualized" (2026-06-16); Tomasz Tunguz "Databricks Widens the Lead on the Yellow Brick Token Path"

findings.claim: ClickHouse (open-source-based challenger positioned against both Snowflake and Databricks, especially for high-concurrency/low-latency analytics workloads) raised $400M at a $15B valuation in January 2026, roughly 2.5x its prior $6.35B valuation from May 2025 — signaling accelerating well-funded new-entrant pressure at the workload edges.
findings.source: Yahoo Finance "Snowflake, Databricks challenger ClickHouse hits $15B valuation"

findings.claim: As of 2025, over 52% of Snowflake's customers also use Databricks, up from ~40% in 2024 — rising dual-platform adoption inside Snowflake's own installed base rather than clean one-way switching either direction.
findings.source: PitchGrade Research "Snowflake vs. Databricks: Revenue Models, Customer Overlap, and IPO Readiness"

findings.claim: Snowflake Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-07-31, reported 2026-09-02): product revenue $1.49B up 37% YoY (accelerated vs prior quarters), net revenue retention rate 126%, 14,554 total customers with 692 net new adds, 828 customers with >$1M annual product revenue (up 27% YoY) — shows Snowflake is still gaining absolute share of enterprise data-platform spend even as Databricks grows faster off a smaller/now-larger base.
findings.source: Snowflake Q2 FY2027 earnings release / SEC 8-K (fy2027q2earnings.htm); CNBC "Snowflake (SNOW) Q2 earnings report 2027"

findings.claim: On the Q2 FY2027 earnings call (2026-09-02), CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy described three reinforcing structural dynamics behind accelerating growth: (1) AI is bringing new workloads onto the platform as enterprises need a governed, unified data foundation, (2) first-party AI products (CoCo coding assistant, CoWork agent platform) are seeing rapid adoption, (3) AI activation is lifting overall platform consumption as customers using AI consume more of the broader data platform — framed by management as a structural multiplier, not a one-off cyclical bump. Cortex Code topped 9,100 accounts (+2,000 in the quarter); CoWork reached 5,800 accounts.
findings.source: Snowflake Q2 FY2027 earnings call transcript / Constellation Research "Snowflake Q2 growth surges on AI and data demand"

findings.claim: Snowflake's own risk-factor disclosure states that customers may continue to optimize consumption, rationalize budgets, and prioritize cash-flow management — including by reducing data retention periods, shortening committed contract durations, and applying auto-suspend/workload-efficiency measures — and that in any given period customer consumption could grow slower than expected, driving revenue-growth volatility. This is management's own acknowledgment that the consumption-based model has a demonstrated cyclical/IT-budget-optimization sensitivity layered on top of the structural AI growth narrative (seen historically during the FY2024 IT-budget-optimization period when growth decelerated sharply from prior years).
findings.source: Snowflake Inc. Form 10-K risk factors (fiscal year 2026, SEC EDGAR); Software Stack Investing historical earnings reviews (FY2024 optimization cycle)

findings.claim: At the broader AI-infrastructure/hyperscaler capex level (adjacent but not identical to Snowflake's own software-consumption demand), independent analysts (e.g. Morningstar) flag risk of AI spending peaking in 2025 with a slowdown emerging in 2026 as macro risk intensifies, ROI questions on hyperscaler AI capex rise, and hedge funds increasingly separate "durable winners from overextended names" within the AI trade rather than treating it as a single basket.
findings.source: Morningstar (via Yahoo Finance "Even the AI gold rush can't stop the chip industry's boom-bust cycle"); Futuriom/HedgeCo AI-capex-fatigue coverage
